name: Conferences and Positive Notes
title: Conferences and Positive Notes
answer: Conferences and positive notes are two family communication practices where AI can help with drafting while the teacher keeps the substance. A teacher can use an approved tool to summarize a short conference and to draft brief positive notes home, then review, personalize and send them, translated if needed. The point is to give families a clear record and to build relationships before hard conversations are needed.

sections.body: Parent conferences are brief, and families often leave without a clear record of what was said, so a teacher can use an approved tool to draft a short summary covering the child's strengths, areas for growth and next steps. Positive notes home serve a different purpose: they build relationships that make difficult conversations easier later, because many parents only hear from school when something is wrong. AI can help draft these short notes, but the teacher adds a specific detail about what the child actually did well. The personal detail is what makes a positive note work, since a generic message that a child is doing great means little, while a note about a child helping a classmate solve a hard problem means a great deal. AI can help with the form, but the teacher supplies the substance.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a school or classroom, a teacher uses an approved tool to draft a brief conference summary that covers the child's strengths, areas for growth and next steps, then reviews and sends it, translated if needed. For positive notes, the teacher uses AI to help draft a short message home, then adds a specific detail about what the child did well before sending it. TalkingPoints makes it easy to send positive notes in the family's language. Names and sensitive details should stay out of any tool that is not covered by a signed agreement. The text does not give separate grade band variations, so the practice applies across ages with the same steps.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no evidence label, study, figure or finding for this idea. It rests on practice rather than research, describing what teachers can do with approved tools and what makes a positive note effective.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: Names and sensitive details should stay out of any tool not covered by a signed agreement. The teacher reviews and sends the summary and the positive notes, so the decision to send and what to include stays with a person. AI can help with the form of a message, but the teacher supplies the substance, meaning the specific detail about the child's success is the teacher's responsibility. Translation support does not remove the teacher's duty to check the message before it goes home.
